implemented_model_facts.nominal_local_net_flux_form: Phi_i = sum_{j in N(i)} S_j q_{j->i} - S_i sum_{k in N(i)} q_{i->k}, with committed orders entering at full transported strength and prospective q containing command-decision and destination-choice probabilities.
implemented_model_facts.executable_flux_correction: For prospective orders q_exec = q_nominal * command_reliability. Already committed orders have passed the reliability draw and retain full weight.

closure_identity.claim: Net flux is a first-moment projection of a higher-dimensional graph source state and is generally non-injective. Equal Phi_i does not imply equal future Phi_i.
derivation: Let z_N(i) contain neighboring formation strength, command state, recruitment/rooted reservoirs, beliefs, footholds, and destination propensities.
The diagnostic flux is a projection Phi_i = h(z_N(i)). Many distinct z_N(i) can map to the same scalar Phi_i.
The next flux satisfies Phi_i(t+dt) = h(T(z_N(i), noise)). If T varies along a level set of h, then equal current Phi_i cannot define a Markov state for future Phi_i.

Therefore scalar-flux closure requires either that h be sufficient on the tested support or that source-state evolution be conditionally identical on each h-level set. The strict closure failures falsify that sufficiency on the tested 30d support.

spatial_markov_blanket.one_step: With adjacent-only relocation, the direct causal source set for next-command incoming movement is the one-hop neighborhood N(i).
spatial_markov_blanket.multi_step: Over repeated relocation/recruitment cycles, information can enter N(i) from N^2(i), then N^3(i), so the spatial support required for finite-horizon closure can expand with horizon.
spatial_markov_blanket.consequence: Reduced closure should be treated as a graph-field/horizon problem, not assumed to be a fixed-dimensional per-locality ODE problem.

falsifiable_predictions: Replacing nominal net flux with command-reliability-weighted executable net flux should reduce transport-driven closure failures if command realizability is the dominant omitted source state.

If executable flux is insufficient, adding one-hop transportable force, rooted stock, and recruitment hazard should reduce transport/reproduction failures if the missing state is the graph Markov blanket.
If one-hop state is sufficient at short horizons but not long horizons, demonstrable non-equivalence should reappear as horizon increases, consistent with an expanding spatial causal cone.
If one-hop state fails immediately even at short horizons, either the source projection remains too coarse or non-movement channels create longer-range coupling.
general_theory_interpretation: A locality can be observationally identical in current stock and net flux while embedded in a different insurgent source network. The distinction is analogous to matching water level and current flow while ignoring the upstream reservoir and valve state: the derivative of the flow remains unidentified.
scientific_guard: The mathematical non-injectivity statement is about the implemented synthetic graph process. Any claim that a real conflict has the same Markov blanket or propagation radius requires historical/empirical validation.
